purpose: Contract governance, SDK distribution and cross-repository compatibility. Not a runtime gateway.

authority: Testagram-native access-token issuance and live-session validation
services.auth: Testagram-native short-lived access JWT; PostgreSQL session/account checks on every protected request; opaque rotating refresh token accepted only by /api/auth/refresh; no Appwrite bearer fallback on end-user routes
services.notes: Backend is the sole public product API and canonical identity authority. Mainline issues native Testagram sessions and checks PostgreSQL session/account state; legacy Appwrite IDs remain only as explicit reconciliation inputs and are not accepted as user bearer credentials. Admin Console staff sessions use the native Backend identity plus the encrypted testagram-staff cookie and PostgreSQL staff-role/MFA records. Registration remains fail-closed until private evidence, email, independent review and provisioning gates are enabled and accepted.

authority: Testagram-native login, refresh, recovery and session restoration
services.auth: Uses Backend-native login and rotating refresh credentials; stores only the refresh token in platform secure storage; access token stays in memory
services.notes: Flutter uses the Testagram-native Backend auth client for login, password recovery/reset, session restore, refresh and logout. It calls only the Backend public API with the short-lived native access token. Applicant and verification-session tokens are limited to their own identity operations; the native password is set only after approved provisioning. No Appwrite JWT is sent by the public client. Flutter must never receive service tokens, storage-provider keys, database credentials or private service URLs.

services.auth: PLATFORM_INTERNAL_TOKEN for protected platform writes; video and notification user routes validate Backend-native access JWTs against live PostgreSQL session/account state; user tokens are never platform service credentials
services.notes: Data Centre PR #66 added the opt-in `media` profile with a separate media database, private `testagram-platform` network, five authenticated lifecycle routes, durable verify/replicate/delete outbox and reconciliation worker. Data Centre PR #67 fixed Compose shell-variable escaping so the disabled profile no longer blocks core production deployment; CI now validates both disabled and enabled profile models and runs the dedicated media service smoke. Backend's typed client and API contract checks cover the five routes. Backend deployment has not yet enabled this profile; `DATA_CENTRE_MEDIA_ENABLED` must remain false until dedicated B2/R2 staging write/read/hash/replication/delete/restore acceptance passes. Keep `FRESH_MEDIA_ENABLED=false` because the separate Fresh API runtime still lacks the canonical Data Centre adapter/metadata-ledger integration. User-aware video and notification routes share the Backend-native JWT format and independently recheck live session, token version, account status, email verification and native-registration state in PostgreSQL. Their TESTAGRAM_AUTH_JWT_SECRET must match the Backend issuer; PLATFORM_INTERNAL_TOKEN and notification/media service credentials remain separate. The legacy Fresh Backend image remains referenced by Data Centre vps/docker-compose.yml and still requires Appwrite endpoint/project/database/server-key settings; it is separately audited as a legacy runtime and must not be removed until production traffic and account cutover are proven.

services.auth: Backend-issued short-lived viewer assertion for private media; separate origin and purge credentials; raw user access JWT is not forwarded as a CDN origin credential
services.notes: Backend PR #223 is merged. It replaces the legacy Nginx cache with the immutable Go CDN image (`sha256:e4c014a043b761d6f84b05d3973a3a6831522b863eef08685b7ca6db17f55ce9`), gives it a persistent bounded cache, private Backend origin, distinct origin/viewer-assertion/purge credentials, cache purge-before-delete, Instabox container verification and external health/readiness/unauthenticated-denial smoke. The PostgreSQL-backed Backend origin matrix, Go security checks, Backend race/static tests and self-hosted Compose validation passed pre-merge. The first production deployment attempt reached the VPS but stopped at Data Centre Compose interpolation; Data Centre PR #67 fixed that defect and the failed deployment job is being rerun. Do not claim live CDN service until that rerun and external HTTPS smoke pass. CDN issues #61/#65 still report `media.testagram.site` serving the older R2 Worker; custom-domain/DNS cutover and rollback are not yet evidenced. Cloudflare deployment/DNS credentials are not available through the current repository integration. CDN viewer assertions are distinct from user access JWTs and from the origin/purge service credentials. CDN never becomes the identity or visibility authority.

authority: signed delivery of Backend-authorized public Create activities
public dereferencing of Backend-canonical ActivityPub Notes
services.auth: Public ActivityPub ingress uses HTTP Signatures; Backend-to-Federation uses a distinct service bearer; Federation-to-Backend uses a different service bearer
services.notes: Backend publishes authorized activities to the private /internal/v1/activities ingress using a dedicated direction-specific service bearer and activity ID idempotency key. Federation authenticates the ingress, verifies Backend actor eligibility, durably enqueues the outbox item and acknowledges 202 only after acceptance. Federation-to-Backend uses a separate bearer. Public routing, inbound activity projections, delivery workers and external-peer interoperability remain gated; durable acceptance is not proof of delivery.

authority: ranking order and ranking scores only
services.notes: Backend submits at most 200 already-authorized candidates to POST /v1/feed/rank and requests at most 50 results. The pinned Backend client and Algorithm OpenAPI agree on the path and API-version/service-bearer headers. Backend rejects unknown/duplicate IDs and rechecks current authorization before hydration. Staging service-authentication, timeout/fallback and load acceptance remain required.
